entities.name: Latent tuberculosis infection
observations: Positive IGRA with no symptoms, normal chest radiograph, and negative sputum evaluation supports TB infection without active disease.
Active tuberculosis must be excluded before preventive therapy.

entities.name: Isoniazid
observations: Daily isoniazid for 6 or 9 months is an accepted alternative regimen for latent TB infection.
Pyridoxine should accompany isoniazid to reduce peripheral neuropathy risk.

entities.name: Rifampin
observations: Four months of daily rifampin is a preferred short-course LTBI regimen in adults without contraindications.
Rifampin monotherapy is preferred over prolonged isoniazid in many guideline-based settings because of completion and safety advantages.

entities.name: Isoniazid with pyridoxine
observations: Isoniazid plus pyridoxine is a conventional answer for treating latent TB infection when an isoniazid regimen is selected.
It is less preferred than short rifamycin-based regimens in current CDC/NTCA guidance, but remains acceptable when rifamycin regimens are unsuitable.
